solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Roman watering-hole provides a mineral

blocks.note: Cinna was a consul of the Roman Republic
a bar is a place for drinking

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman drinking spot turns out to be a source of some useful mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Roman watering-hole' reads as one thing, a Roman bath or tavern, but it splits into a named Roman and a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the red ore of mercury, a naturally occurring crystalline mineral used for vermilion pigment.

clue.text: No victory, with commander in retreat as timid type

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a match that nobody wins is a draw
OC is Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A general who retreats without winning is branded a timid sort.
explanation.walkthrough: OC, Officer Commanding, is a standard military abbreviation; the whole string of result plus officer is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lacking courage, who shrinks from danger, is a timid type by any ordinary description.

clue.text: Partners embracing single hour of prayer

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap arms around, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: North and South are partners at the bridge table
single means one

explanation.surface: Couples hug a lone worshipper at a set time of devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, and North-South form a partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: In the monastic day the ninth hour office, said around mid-afternoon, is one of the canonical times of worship.

clue.text: Forest not all green: no grass coming up

indicators.note: not all of the words are used, only a run of letters from inside them
in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A woodland that is patchy, with no grass growing through the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'green no grass' backwards and ARGONNE is there. 'not all green' suggests a partly brown forest, but it tells you only part of the letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonne is a wooded region in north-eastern France, famous as a First World War battlefield.

clue.text: Given a number in the theatre?

definitions.text: Given a number in the theatre?

blocks.clueFragment: Given a number in the theatre?
blocks.note: surface reading: handed a song or act to perform on stage

blocks.clueFragment: Given a number in the theatre?
blocks.note: setter's reading: made numb before surgery in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is really numb-er, something that numbs, and 'the theatre' is the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient put under before surgery has been rendered insensible to pain, which is what numbing drugs do.

clue.text: One dedicated old boy no longer with us

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A devoted former pupil has passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a person offered to or dedicated to religious life, often a lay member attached to a monastery.

clue.text: Happens to take risk on fateful day

blocks.note: a bet is a risk taken on an outcome
the Ides of March was the day Julius Caesar was murdered

explanation.surface: Something occurs when you gamble on a day of doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the day after the risk. The Ides is the fateful day of Caesar's assassination, 'Beware the Ides of March'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb, as in 'woe betide you', means to befall someone or occur to them.

clue.text: Arrest happened originally outside front of restaurant

indicators.note: done originally means done in a novel way, so the letters take a new arrangement
the front of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept
one thing placed outside another surrounds it, so a letter sits within

blocks.note: used as fodder, letters to be rearranged
the first letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: A police arrest that took place just outside the front of a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' seems to mean 'at first' and pull a first letter, but it rearranges the whole word, which then surrounds the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Police apprehend a suspect when they seize and take them into custody, the same as an arrest.

clue.text: Disguising the dénouement to keep company enthralled

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the dénouement is the ending of a story
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A writer hides the twist ending to keep the audience spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending holds the company, and 'enthralled' just reinforces the picture of the company held captive.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a message into code conceals its meaning from outsiders, a form of disguise.

clue.text: One may have champagne, say, to secure maiden coming round

indicators.note: coming round something means going all the way about it, enclosing it

blocks.note: to secure a prize is to win it
EG, for example, is what 'say' means
a maiden is a young girl

explanation.surface: A suitor might offer champagne to win over a girl who comes to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the example word here, not speech; the winning and the girl go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemmed vessel for drinking holds wine, and champagne is one such drink it might contain.

clue.text: There’s a way in which one becomes aggressive

definitions.text: There’s a way in which one becomes aggressive

blocks.clueFragment: There’s a way in which one becomes aggressive
blocks.note: surface reading: there is a method by which a person turns hostile

blocks.clueFragment: There’s a way in which one becomes aggressive
blocks.note: setter's reading: a way is a road, and it is in the road that this brawler does his fighting

explanation.walkthrough: 'a way' is not a method but a thoroughfare, and the aggressive one is someone who brawls out in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough who brawls in public roads, or anyone combative with no rules, is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Matter is poisonous, quietly knocking out ten

indicators.note: knocking one out and bringing another in swaps a letter for a different one

blocks.note: toxic means poisonous
p, piano, means quietly in music
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A poison works silently, knocking out ten victims.
explanation.walkthrough: The P takes the place of the X in the poisonous word.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is the matter being talked about, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: With Republican, one celebrates revolts

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
I is the Roman numeral for one
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Alongside a Republican, someone celebrates popular uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolts' looks like a verb but it is a plural noun, rebellions.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular uprisings against rulers are called revolts, as in the Easter Rising.

clue.text: Communist leader as one who joined spurious league?

blocks.note: a Red is a communist
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A party leader is cast as a member of some bogus association.
explanation.walkthrough: The league is Conan Doyle's 'The Red-Headed League', a Sherlock Holmes story in which a sham society recruits ginger-haired men.
explanation.definitionFit: Only people with ginger hair could join the fake league in the Holmes story, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: The Leninist managed to capture city and country

indicators.note: managed means handled or worked on, so the letters are reworked into a new order
to capture is to take something in and hold it

blocks.note: used as fodder, letters to be rearranged
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A Leninist revolutionary succeeded in seizing a city and then a whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The City in crosswords is the City of London, whose postal district is EC; those letters join the Leninist ones before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small principality between Switzerland and Austria, a sovereign state in its own right.

clue.text: Car and cow collide finally

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so its last letter is kept

blocks.note: the Limousin is a French breed of beef cattle
the last letter of collide

explanation.surface: A car and a cow end up crashing into each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The cow is a specific breed, named after the Limousin region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: A large luxurious chauffeur-driven motor vehicle is a type of car.

clue.text: Good sort, this person’s high-class, with endless desire for encouragement

indicators.note: something endless has lost its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a good sort is a saint, abbreviated ST
this person is the speaker, I, and 'I'm' is 'I is' contracted
U means upper-class
lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A decent person says they are posh and need endless craving to feel encouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British usage from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U. 'this person's' reads as a possessive but is the contraction 'I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that spurs a person to act or makes them try harder is a stimulus, an incentive or spur.

clue.text: The enemy being forgotten about for ages?

blocks.note: 'Time, the old enemy' is a stock phrase
something forgotten is out of mind

explanation.surface: An old foe has been neglected and ignored for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is the enemy of everything, which is why 'the enemy' can mean it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means for longer than anyone can remember, that is, for a very long while.

clue.text: Old desire restricting you, having limited vision

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so one piece is confined within another

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a need is a desire
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: An old craving has kept you narrow-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: The old form of 'you' sits between the last two letters of the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with sight in only one eye has a restricted field of view.

clue.text: More unstable, doing nothing almost, after hospital admission

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole, so the last letter is left off
an admission is a letting in, so one piece is let into another

blocks.note: inert means inactive
san is short for sanatorium

explanation.surface: A patient has become more unhinged after being admitted to a psychiatric ward with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: SAN, a sanatorium, is the school or clinic sickbay; it is let into the shortened idle word.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word for mentally deranged means further from stable or sound mind.

clue.text: Session with some late arrivals?

blocks.note: surface reading: a meeting that some people turned up to late
setter's reading: a sitting at which the dead, the late, are supposed to appear

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not tardy, so the arrivals are spirits of the departed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering at which a medium tries to contact the spirits of dead people is exactly this sitting.

clue.text: Cats — those in need of medical treatment, it seems

definitions.text: those in need of medical treatment, it seems

blocks.note: first meaning: cats valued for catching rodents

blocks.clueFragment: those in need of medical treatment, it seems
blocks.note: second, jokey meaning: people who use a medical officer, abbreviated MO, as the word appears to say if split after two letters

explanation.surface: Some cats look as though they need to see the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is a medical officer; the word for cats that catch mice looks, split after its second letter, like people who use one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats kept to catch vermin in barns and houses are called by this name after their prey.

clue.text: Develop mentally, say, after good education initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken
after means following, so the piece it governs is sent second, behind the others

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the first letter of education
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A child's mind grows, so to speak, after a good schooling early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the saying word behind the two letters from good and education.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides carrying young in the womb, to gestate means to form and develop an idea slowly in the mind.

clue.text: Getting rid of a whole lot of players no good

blocks.note: taken as written
a team of eleven, as in cricket or football, is an XI
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A manager clears out a whole squad of useless players.
explanation.walkthrough: A whole team, the full eleven, is written XI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe someone is to dismiss them or cut them, so the participle means removing or disposing of.

clue.text: People taking position about sex

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: the lay of the land is its position or arrangement
it is a coy word for sex, or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Folk adopt a stance on sexual matters.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex or sex appeal is a crossword favourite, from the old sense of 'it girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary members of a church, as opposed to clergy, are the lay people collectively.

clue.text: School punishment — what could make Eton end it?

indicators.note: asking what could be made from some letters invites building a new word from them

blocks.note: used as fodder, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Which school penalty might be so bad that a famous school gives it up?
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school, so the school word supports the surface while feeding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a pupil behind after classes as a penalty is the standard sanction in British and American schools.

clue.text: Swift, see, crossing river to the west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west is going right to left, so the letters run backwards
crossing means spanning over, so one piece stretches across another

blocks.note: to spy is to see
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A swift bird is spotted flying over a river heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is capitalised as if the bird; the Dee flows through Wales, England and Scotland in different rivers of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift as an adjective means fast, and the answer is a common synonym for quick.

clue.text: No amateur baddy to hold off for a while

blocks.note: a professional is not an amateur
a rogue is a villain

explanation.surface: A professional villain means to delay things for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is mostly used of parliaments, which are suspended between sessions without being dissolved.
explanation.definitionFit: It means to discontinue a session or defer something, postponing it to a later date.
